pointers.sentence: `django.utils.translation.trans_real.translation` keeps a dictionary, `_translations`, from a language's code as it was given to its `DjangoTranslation`, and makes the object the first time the code is asked for (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:translation`).
Unlike its parent, it reads many files into one catalogue (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:DjangoTranslation`).
`DjangoTranslation.__init__` builds the object in this order (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:DjangoTranslation.__init__`):

Then `DjangoTranslation._init_translation_catalog` reads Django's own catalogue from the `locale` directory beside the module the settings object's `__module__` names: `"django.conf"`, where `LazySettings` is defined, not the project's settings module; so `django/conf/locale/`.

`DjangoTranslation._new_gnu_trans` hands a directory to the standard library's `gettext.translation`, with the domain, the language's locale name from `to_locale`, and `fallback=True`, so that a directory without the file gives a `gettext.NullTranslations` rather than an error (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:DjangoTranslation._new_gnu_trans`).
`DjangoTranslation.merge` passes over a result with no catalogue (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:DjangoTranslation.merge`).
Its docstring gives its purpose: to keep catalogues whose plural equations differ apart (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:TranslationCatalog`).

The example's Dutch translations hold two, the office's above Django's, though both files have the formula `"nplurals=2; plural=(n != 1);"` (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:TranslationCatalog.update`).

`DjangoTranslation._add_fallback` sets none for `LANGUAGE_CODE` itself, nor for a code beginning `"en"`; the comment's reason for the second is that an English catalogue is empty, so an English lookup would always fall through to the default language (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:DjangoTranslation._add_fallback`).
`to_language` goes back, in lower case with a hyphen (`django/utils/translation/__init__.py:to_locale`, `django/utils/translation/__init__.py:to_language`).

`django.utils.translation.trans_real.all_locale_paths` lists where a catalogue may be: Django's own directory, those of `LOCALE_PATHS`, and the `locale` directory of each application that has one (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:all_locale_paths`).

`django.utils.translation.reloader.watch_for_translation_changes` has the reloader watch every `.mo` file under the `locale` directory where the process runs, under each application's that is not Django's own, and under each directory of `LOCALE_PATHS` (`django/utils/translation/reloader.py:watch_for_translation_changes`).
It returns true, so the server goes on in the same process ([The autoreloader](../commands/autoreload.md)) (`django/utils/translation/reloader.py:translation_file_changed`).

An override of `LANGUAGE_CODE` leaves it, and forgets only the default translation and the active one, so a language built before keeps the old default behind it ([Overriding settings](../startup/overrides.md)) (`django/test/signals.py:language_changed`, `django/test/signals.py:update_installed_apps`).
